cards.t: Decide what you want from dating right now. Think about marriage and roughly when, and about children. Write your answers down before you talk to anyone.
Pick two things to try this month for meeting serious men. Church groups, classes, running clubs and volunteering put you in the same room every week.
cards.l: Open the Meet Marriage Minded Men Checklist

cards.t: Write down everything you think you want in a man, without editing. Twenty items is normal at this stage.
Cross out anything you would stay in the relationship despite. That is a preference. What is left is your short list.
Rewrite one item as something you can see. "He keeps the commitments he makes to me, even small ones" is easier to check than "he must be responsible."
Most people have three to five non negotiables. If you would stay anyway, it is a preference, and you are allowed those too.
Watch how he treats the waiter, the gateman and his mother. Character shows most where there is nothing to gain.
Notice whether he does what he says, again and again. The guide calls consistency the strongest early signal.
Next time you say no or not yet, watch what he does. Sulking or pressing tells you something. Hearing it without fuss tells you something too.
Ask him what he is looking for right now. A specific answer with a timeline helps. "Just going with the flow" for three months is also an answer.
Ask two or three questions per conversation, and answer them yourself too. That way it does not feel like an interview.
Ask when he was last in a relationship and what ended it. Listen for whether he can name one thing that was his fault.
Ask if he wants children, and roughly when. The "when" matters most.
Ask how he handles money and who he supports. Black tax is real and supporting family is fine. Not telling you about it is the problem.
Ask what an argument looks like for him. He may shout, go silent, walk out or talk it through. Then check it against what you have seen.
Play Delulu or Clear-Eyed. You pick what you would do in ten talking stage situations, like he watched your story and did not reply.
A talking stage usually runs a few weeks to about three months. If you cannot say what this is after eight to twelve weeks of near daily contact, it may be idling.
Ask "what are we?" once, plainly, around week eight to twelve. His answer, or his dodge, is information.
Before you ask him "so what are we?", answer five questions for yourself. What do you want, and what will you do if his answer is not what you hope?
If plans are always short notice and you are rarely part of anything scheduled, try the Situationship Checker. Six questions give you a read and words to ask where this is going.
A situationship is a relationship in everything but name. If the two of you would describe it differently, that is the sign.
Notice how you feel after you see him. Early weeks of a real relationship are uncertain but they settle you. If you feel more anxious every time, write that down.
Early red flags are small and repeated. Every ex is crazy. Your no gets negotiated. He is vague about the basics. Pick one and watch whether it repeats.
One red flag, owned and changed afterwards, is a bad day. Three or more together is a pattern, and the guide says to act on it.
Tick what you have actually seen him do, from the green list and the red list, and see them counted with one next step.
cards.l: Open the Green and Red Flags Checker

cards.t: Call five everyday situations green flag, let's talk or red flag in Red Flag Radar, then see where your read matches ours.
Couple Alignment asks each of you the same 12 questions on money, children, family, where to live, faith at home and work after children. Then you see where you agree.
Ask how close he is to his family and how much they decide. Then ask yourself the same thing.
When family keeps asking when you will marry, remember that knowing what you want is the easier part. Holding onto it is harder, so read your own list again before you answer them.
Take the Are You Ready for Love quiz. Eight questions on what you want, your standards and whether family pressure, age or fear is driving who you date. You cannot fail it.
cards.l: Take the Ready for Love quiz

cards.t: Day 1 is the first day of bleeding. Log it in the Period Tracker on the day it starts. Three logged periods give you your own average cycle.
Count cycle days from the first day of your last period. The day bleeding stops has no part in the sum, and every calculator and app starts at day 1.
Write down the first day of every period. A doctor will want your last three or four dates, and so will an antenatal clinic.
The National Health Service advises 400 micrograms of folic acid a day, ideally from three months before you try. You cannot reliably get that amount from food alone.
Ask a doctor before you start folic acid if you have sickle cell disease or do not know your genotype. Some women are advised a higher dose on prescription.
The fertile window is about six days: the five days before ovulation plus the day itself. Sperm can live up to about five days inside the body.
On a short cycle the window can start soon after bleeding ends. The days right after a period are not a time to assume you cannot conceive.
Day 14 only fits a 28 day cycle. The National Health Service puts normal cycles at 21 to 35 days, so ovulation can move by two weeks.
Ovulation is better estimated backwards from your next period. The National Health Service puts it at around 10 to 16 days before.
Add your last period start and usual cycle length to the Ovulation Calculator. It gives a window and not a date, because even the steadier half of a cycle has a six day spread.
Cervical mucus that is clear, stretchy and slippery like raw egg white may mean the window is open now. It is the one common sign that points forwards.
A small rise in resting temperature comes after ovulation. It helps you learn your pattern, but it cannot help you catch this month.
A one sided twinge is felt by some women and not by many. It is not reliable enough to plan around on its own.
Most of the fertile window sits before ovulation. Sex every two or three days across the cycle covers it without checking a chart first.
There is no evidence that saving up improves the odds, and long gaps can work against you. Regular works better than strategic.
Ovulation predictor strips pick up the hormone surge a day or two before release. A clinic scan can see it directly. Both tell you more than any calendar.
Illness, travel, stress and weight change can all move ovulation. Treat every date on a screen as an estimate.
Read each date as the middle of a range. Cycles that vary by three or four days are ordinary, so your real days can sit three or four days either side.
Folic acid protects a pregnancy once there is one. It does not make conception more likely, and it does not treat hormonal imbalance.
The neural tube closes in the first month, often before a woman knows she is pregnant. That is why folic acid starts before you try.
Stop alcohol and smoking, and ask him to stop too. Both affect fertility and an early pregnancy you do not yet know about.
Review every medicine and supplement with a pharmacist, herbal products included. Some need changing well before you try.
Know your genotype and your blood group before you try. Dental work is also far simpler now than later.
Aim for a steady weight. Being very underweight or very overweight can affect fertility, and a crash diet while trying works against you.
Fertility is a two person job. Ask him to get a semen analysis early. It is cheap and quick, and testing one person tells you about one person.
See a doctor if your cycles are very irregular, shorter than 21 days, longer than 35, or have stopped. Severe period pain or pain during sex also needs a visit.
Talk to a doctor after twelve months of trying, or six months if you are over 35. Go together and ask for a semen analysis at the first visit.
Your next day 1 is your last first day plus your usual cycle length. Log it the day it starts. A late date on the screen tells you nothing a test cannot tell you better.
Very early. A test may only just be positive. Start folic acid if you have not, 400 micrograms a day through week 12.
Register at an antenatal clinic early, before you start to show. This first visit is called booking.
The baby's major organs are forming. Nausea and tiredness are common, and some women feel almost nothing, and that is normal too.
cards.l: Open the Week by Week Tracker

cards.t: Booking checks blood pressure, blood group, genotype and anaemia. They help most when there is time to act on them.
Take the malaria doses your clinic gives you and sleep under a treated net. The World Health Organization lists pregnant women at higher risk of severe malaria.
Your first scan is often somewhere around weeks 8 to 12. It dates the pregnancy more accurately than counting yourself.
Raw or undercooked meat, unpasteurised milk and liver are on the list to avoid. Cook everything through, and skip alcohol.
You do not need to eat for two. Aim for at least five portions of fruit and vegetables a day, and wash them to remove soil.
This is the end of the first trimester. Sickness often begins to ease, and the folic acid advice runs through week 12.
cards.l: Open the Week by Week Tracker

cards.t: The second trimester begins. Many women feel more energy, and you may start to show.
The second trimester is usually the easiest stretch. Use the energy to plan the birth, sort the money and settle who is coming for omugwo.
Tiger nut, garden egg and cloves in your jollof are fine. We would leave bitter kola alone. Concentrated clove oil is a different thing.
Lipton and every other tea count toward the caffeine limit of 200mg a day. Drink tea an hour away from meals, because it lowers how much iron you absorb.
Bottled kunun aya from the roadside is soaked, ground and sold unrefrigerated. Make it at home with clean water, keep it cold and drink it the same day.
The detailed scan of how your baby is growing usually comes around weeks 18 to 22. Tick the questions you want to ask before you go.
Around now many women feel the first movements, often between weeks 18 and 24, and earlier in a second pregnancy.
cards.l: Open the Week by Week Tracker

cards.t: The anomaly scan usually happens near week 20. Ask what it costs and whether the price includes the report and a printout before you book.
Anaemia is common in pregnancy across Nigeria, so take iron seriously. Keep tea away from meals you are eating for iron.
Do not take agbo or herbal mixtures without asking your doctor. In one study of 595 pregnant women in Nigeria, more than two thirds had used herbal medicines.
A fever or an illness that is not settling is a reason to call your clinic the same day. Do not treat it yourself with tablets, agbo or herbal mixtures first.
Write your birth preferences down: who is with you, pain relief, movement and feeding. Plans can change on the day, and that is normal.
A newborn needs far less than the baby shop and the aunty at church will tell you. Tick the Newborn Essentials Checklist before you buy.
Buy the baby cot, clothes and diapers first and leave the rest until after the birth. If you plan to breastfeed, you do not need to stock up on bottles.
Decide who takes you to hospital and how you will get there at 2am. Working it out during contractions is how avoidable delays happen.
The third trimester begins. Learn your baby's pattern of movement and report any change the same day. Do not wait for your next appointment.
Backache, heartburn, breathlessness and broken sleep are the usual complaints now. Avoid lifting heavy objects and wear flat shoes.
Start thinking about your hospital bag. The checklist has one list for you, one for the baby and one for whoever is with you.
The World Health Organization recommends at least eight antenatal contacts. Each one catches something that is cheaper to fix early. Take your questions with you.
Call your midwife or maternity unit immediately if the baby is moving less than usual. Do not wait until the next day.
Take your birth plan to your next visit. Your team will always put your safety and your baby's first, and plans often change on the day.
Bleeding, severe pain, fever, a bad headache with blurred sight, or fluid leaking means see a doctor or go to hospital. If you are unsure, call.
Ask your hospital for its own packing list at antenatal booking, and follow it as well as ours.
Your hospital bag should be packed by about now. Know the route and decide who takes you, so nobody works it out during contractions.
Full term from here, so baby could arrive any time. Know the signs of labour and when to go in.
Read your birth plan once more and print it for the hospital. Birth can change, and that is normal.
Check the basics are ready: a baby cot with a firm, flat mattress and a mosquito net, clothes, diapers and a way to feed.
Contact your hospital or midwife if your waters break, contractions are strong and regular, you bleed, or the baby is moving less. It is always fine to call.
Bleeding, called lochia, is heaviest this week, so you need maternity pads. If a pad soaks in minutes, or the bleeding feels like gushing, go to hospital.
Bleeding lightens and changes colour from red to brown to a pale discharge. Heavier bleeding again, fever, foul smelling discharge or pain that gets worse needs a doctor.
Ask visitors and whoever came for omugwo to take the kitchen and the laundry. Holding the baby comes second. Tick what would help most.
Many women feel a little more themselves around weeks 4 to 5. Short walks help. Hard exercise has to wait while the core and pelvic floor heal.
Enter your delivery date and whether it was vaginal or caesarean. The calculator shows your current stage and the date each stage starts.
The six week check is about you. Write your questions down first, because the appointment is short. Ask about pain, sex, contraception and feeding.
You can become pregnant again as soon as three weeks after birth, even if you are breastfeeding and your periods have not returned. Raise contraception at your check.
Six weeks is not a finish line. Blood pressure problems, clots and infection can start after week six. See a doctor for fever, worsening pain or a hot, painful, swollen calf.
Omugwo usually runs one to three months, and one to two months is typical for a mother going back to work. The first six weeks matter most.
If you had a caesarean, hold off on driving, exercise, sex and lifting anything heavier than your baby for six weeks or so. Restart each one only when it feels comfortable.
Sex can hurt for months, and leaking urine when you sneeze is common and treatable. Tell your doctor instead of putting up with either.
Most women feel physically recovered between six and eight weeks, and a caesarean takes longer. Hair may fall out in handfuls around month three or four, and it grows back.
A baby under three months with a temperature of 38°C or higher needs hospital now. So does a baby who cannot feed, has a fit or is hard to wake.
cards.l: Read when to go to hospital

cards.t: The 6 week visit is three injections and two doses by mouth. Feeding straight after settles most babies faster than anything else.
The 10 week visit is two injections and two doses by mouth, and the 14 week visit follows. Add your baby's date of birth and each visit shows the date it falls due.
Put your baby on the back for every nap and every night sleep, on a firm, flat mattress in a separate baby cot in your room. Nothing else goes in the cot.
Pick your baby's age to see what many babies do around then. Every baby moves at their own pace, so mention any worry at your next clinic visit.
Solids start at around six months, when your baby can sit and hold their head steady, get food to their mouth and swallow it. Milk is still the main meal.
Start with one food at a time, soft and unseasoned: ripe banana, pawpaw, sweet potato, pap or mashed beans. Take your baby's portion out before the seasoning goes in.
Leave out salt, including stock cubes, and leave out sugar. Give no honey before one year. Whole nuts and hard chunks are choking hazards.
The 9 month visit gives the measles and rubella vaccine, yellow fever and meningitis A. If you expect to travel, ask the clinic for the yellow card then.
Before crawling turns into climbing, keep kerosene, bleach, medicines and chemicals in their original containers, locked away. Never put kerosene in a water or soft drink bottle.
Turn pot handles to the wall and keep hot drinks beyond the table's edge. Never carry your baby with hot tea or soup. Run the generator outside, about 6 metres from windows and doors.
At 12 months vitamin A is given by mouth. Tick the visit off in the Vaccination Tracker, and photograph both sides of the clinic card.

years.t: The 15 month visit gives the second measles and rubella dose. Add your child's date of birth in the Vaccination Tracker and check which visits are done.
A child can drown quickly and silently in a small amount of water. Empty every bucket after use, cover wells and stay beside a young child near water.
Keep groundnuts, seeds, whole grapes, hard food and small objects away from children under four. Cut food small and have your child sit to eat.
Write your questions for the next clinic visit before you go. After a long wait it is easy to forget half of them.
